BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p269/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p269/r1.speaker: الفخر الرازي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p269/r1.claim: Al-Rāzī and al-Nīsābūrī count preserving the rhyme among the reasons the second-person kāf is omitted from ‘wa-mā qalā.’
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p269/r1.anchor: وعدّ "الفخر الرازي" من وجوه حذف الكاف رعاية الفاصلة.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p269/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p269/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p269/r2.claim: She rejects rhyme as the explanation: the sūra has no thāʾ-ending, and even contains no thāʾ, so a forced substitute for fa-ḥaddith would not fit a rhyme pattern.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p269/r2.anchor: ولو كان البيان القرآني يتعلق بهذا الملحظ اللفظي فحسب، لما عدل عن رعاية الفاصلة في الآيات بعدها

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p269/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p269/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p269/r3.claim: The omitted kāf avoids directly telling the Prophet ‘you are hated’: qalā carries harsh senses of rejection and intense enmity, while waddʿa evokes a loving farewell and hoped-for return.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p269/r3.anchor: تقتضيه حساسية مرهفة بالغة الدقة واللطف، هي ما تحاشى خطابه رسوله المصطفى، في موقف الإيناس، بصريح القول: وما قلاك

BURSEVI:v10p350/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p350/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p350/r6.claim: “Your Lord has not forsaken you” answers the oath; t-w-d-ʿ intensifies leave, and the phrase means God neither abandoned nor lowered Muhammad from revelation, nearness, and honor.
BURSEVI:v10p350/r6.anchor: جواب القسم والتوديع مبالغة في الوداع وهو الترك

BURSEVI:v10p350/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p350/r7.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v10p350/r7.claim: Al-Raghib traces farewell to praying that God grant the traveler ease and safety, which became a customary leave-taking and then a metaphor for abandonment in the verse.
BURSEVI:v10p350/r7.anchor: أن يدعو للمسافر بأن يتحمل الله عنه

BURSEVI:v10p350/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p350/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p350/r8.claim: The inward allusion is that the Lord never abandons the one He nurtures.
BURSEVI:v10p350/r8.anchor: وإشارة إلى أن الرب لا يترك المربوب

BURSEVI:v10p350/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p350/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p350/r9.claim: “Nor did He hate” means that God did not detest him.
BURSEVI:v10p350/r9.anchor: أي وما أبغضك والأبغاض دشمن داشتن

QASHANI:93:3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:93:3/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:93:3/r1.claim: The oath is by light and darkness, the enduring foundations of human being and the two worlds; God did not abandon the Prophet in light while love remained but Essence was veiled.
QASHANI:93:3/r1.anchor: بالنور والظلمة الصرفة القارة على حالها الذين هما أصل الوجود الإنساني

QASHANI:93:3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:93:3/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:93:3/r2.claim: Nor did God reject him in darkness, leaving him with the cosmos without love, veiled from God and His qualities and acts.
QASHANI:93:3/r2.anchor: وما قلاك في عالم الظلمة والوقوف مع الكون بلا محبة وشوق

QASHANI:93:3/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:93:3/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:93:3/r3.claim: The beloved who receives early disclosure may be returned to the veil after witnessing unity, intensifying longing and dissolving ego before the final unveiling, whose savor is fuller.
QASHANI:93:3/r3.anchor: ليشتد شوقه ويلطف سره وتذوب أنائيته بنار الشوق ثم فتح طريقه

QASHANI:93:3/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:93:3/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:93:3/r4.claim: During this concealment, Muhammad climbed mountains to seek direct sight; when his strength failed, the veil lifted and he descended.
QASHANI:93:3/r4.anchor: وكان صلى الله عليه وسلم في هذا الاحتجاب يصعد الجبال ليرى بنفسه

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p353/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p353/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p353/r2.claim: The discourse moves from day and night as models of developmental trials, to reassurance, promised better times, examples of past divine help, and duties arising from those favours.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p353/r2.anchor: Following is the sequence of the discourse

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p356/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p356/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p356/r2.claim: The oaths make the complementary pattern a proof: just as day and night are both needed, alternating ease, hardship, joy, and sorrow train the soul.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p356/r2.anchor: just as in this world the heat and light of the sun are essential and so are the darkness and stillness of the night

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p356/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p356/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p356/r3.claim: God tests whether people respond to good times with gratitude and hard times with patience; the Prophet’s opposition and scant resources are training, not abandonment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p356/r3.anchor: the Almighty tests a person whether he becomes thankful in good times and patient in hard ones

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p356/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p356/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p356/r4.claim: For brevity, the oath’s answer states only the reassurance the Prophet most needed: his present hardship does not mean God is indifferent or displeased.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p356/r4.anchor: only that part of the assurance has found mention

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p357/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p357/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p357/r1.claim: The Prophet feared that his own mistakes had intensified Quraysh hostility and angered God; waiting for revelation could deepen the worry, though revelation comes according to divine wisdom.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p357/r1.anchor: became worried that perhaps some of his own errors

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p357/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p357/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p357/r2.claim: This assurance addresses the Prophet’s private anxiety about his mission and revelation, a concern also discussed in Sūrah Ṭāhā and Sūrah al-Qiyāmah.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p357/r2.anchor: Those who would like to know the details

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p357/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p357/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p357/r3.claim: Islahi rejects the claim that the verse answered a disbelievers’ taunt: they denied revelation and could not know of any pause in it, while the Prophet never stopped preaching.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p357/r3.anchor: It is not necessary that this verse had been revealed in response to the taunt of the disbelievers that the Lord of this person had forsaken him

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p379#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p379#2/r1.speaker: جندب بن سفيان البجلي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p379#2/r1.claim: When Gabriel was delayed, polytheists said Muhammad had been abandoned; this verse was revealed in response.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p379#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عيينة عن الأسود بن قيس قال سمعت جندب بن سفيان البجلي يقول أبطأ جبريل عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال المشركون قد ودع محمد فأنزل الله تعالى ﴿ ما ودعك ربك وما قلى ﴾

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p379#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p379#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p379#2/r2.claim: Qatada likewise says Gabriel delayed and the polytheists claimed the Lord had abandoned Muhammad, prompting the verse.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p379#2/r2.anchor: عن معمر في قوله تعالى ﴿ ما ودعك ربك وما قلى ﴾ قال أبطأ عنه جبريل فقال المشركون قد قلاه ربه

QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r5.claim: God did not stop revelation from Muhammad or hate him; this answered Meccans when Gabriel's visit was delayed for several days.
QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r5.anchor: ما قطع عنك الوحي وما أبغضك

QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r6.claim: Reports differ on Gabriel's absence: forty days, twelve days, or twenty-five days.
QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r6.anchor: وقيل : احتبس عنه جبريل أربعين يوما ، وقيل : اثني عشر يوما ، وقيل : خمسة وعشرين يوما

QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r7.claim: One account says a Jewish question about Dhul-Qarnayn and the People of the Cave delayed the answer after Muhammad promised one without saying God willing.
QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r7.anchor: أن يهوديا سأله عن قصة ذي القرنين وأصحاب الكهف

SULAMI:v2p400#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p400#2/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p400#2/r1.claim: God did not veil the Prophet from nearness when He sent him to people.
SULAMI:v2p400#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء رحمه الله : ما حجبك عن قربه حين بعثك إلى خلقه

SULAMI:v2p400#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p400#2/r2.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p400#2/r2.claim: God did not neglect the Prophet after choosing him.
SULAMI:v2p400#2/r2.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمه الله : ما أهملك بعد أن اصطفاك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p495/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p495/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p495/r3.claim: The surah is Meccan and follows the previous mention of the most pious, the Prophet, by recounting God's favors to him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p495/r3.anchor: هذه السورة مكية. ولما ذكر فيما قبلها وسيجنبها الأتقى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p495/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p495/r4.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p495/r4.claim: The majority read waddaʿaka with a doubled dāl; ʿUrwa, Hishām, and others read it light, meaning God did not leave him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p495/r4.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور ما ودعك بتشديد الدال وعروة بن الزبير وابنه هشام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p495/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p495/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p495/r5.claim: In elevated Arabic, taraka and its forms normally replace wadaʿa and wadhara, though the latter forms are attested; tawdīʿ intensifies leaving someone at separation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p495/r5.anchor: واستغنت العرب في فصيح كلامها بترك عن ودع ووذر، وعن اسم فاعلهما بتارك،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p495/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p495/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p495/r6.claim: Qalā means hated; the common imperfect is yaqlī, while Ṭayyiʾ has taʿlī. The object is omitted in qalā, āwā, hadā, and aghnā because it is understood as the Prophet.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p495/r6.anchor: وما قلى: ما أبغضك، واللغة الشهيرة في مضارع قلى يقلي،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p495/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p495/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p495/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and others report that delayed revelation distressed the Prophet in Mecca; Umm Jamīl said his devil had left him, and the surah then came down.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p495/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس وغيره: أبطأ الوحي مرة على الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو بمكة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p495/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p495/r8.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p495/r8.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says Gabriel withheld revelation because a puppy and dog were in the Prophet's house.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p495/r8.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم: إنما احتبس عنه جبريل عليه السلام لجر وكلب كان في بيته.

FARRA:v3p273#2/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p273#2/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p273#2/r2.claim: The revelation paused for fifteen nights, so the polytheists claimed the Lord had abandoned or disliked Muḥammad; the answer omits the second kaf in wa-mā qalā, as Arabic can avoid repeating a pronoun.
FARRA:v3p273#2/r2.anchor: نزلت في احتباس الوحي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم خمس عشرة

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p531#8/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p531#8/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p531#8/r1.claim: Wa-mā qalā means “He did not hate you.”

MAJAZ:v2p302/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p302/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p302/r3.claim: Waddaʿaka derives from farewell, while the lighter form wadaʿaka is from wadaʿtu/yadaʿu.
MAJAZ:v2p302/r3.anchor: «ما ودعك» (3) من التوديع وما ودعك مخففة من ودعت تدعه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r1.claim: Wadaʿ originally invokes a prayer for a departing traveler to have ease and safety, then came to mean bidding farewell and finally leaving generally.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r1.anchor: وودع من التوديع وهو في الأصل من الدعة وهو أن تدعو للمسافر بأن يدفع الله تعالى عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r2.speaker: البحر والكشاف
ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r2.claim: They take tawdīʿ as an emphatic form of leaving, since one who bids farewell has made a marked departure.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r2.anchor: وفي البحر والكشاف التوديع مبالغة في الودع أي الترك لأن من ودعك مفارقا فقد بالغ

ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r3.claim: An objection says this reading only denies emphatic abandonment; replies are that the emphasis belongs either to the claim made or to the negation itself.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r3.anchor: قيل وعليه يلزم أن يكون المنفي الترك المبالغ فيه دون أصل الترك مع أن الظاهر نفي ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r4.claim: Another reading makes the phrase mean that God did not cut the Prophet off, using farewell as a tender metaphor for leaving; al-Mutanabbī's poem illustrates farewell between beloved people.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r4.anchor: وقيل أن المعنى ما قطعك قطع المودع على أن التوديع مستعارة تبعية للترك

ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r5.claim: Critics object that this metaphor does not answer the mockers; replies say they may have used the phrase sarcastically or that the revelation addresses its literal implication.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r5.anchor: وتعقب بأنه على هذا لا يكون ردا لما قاله المشركون لأنهم لم يقولوا ودعه ربه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r6.claim: A further reading denies even the kind of abandonment that would injure the Prophet's rank, and thereby more emphatically denies the mockers' allegation.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r6.anchor: ولما كان المقصود إيناسه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم وإزالة وحشته عليه الصلاة والسلام جيء بما يتضمن نفي

ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r7.claim: The author thinks the polytheists spoke mockingly, whatever sense of abandonment they intended, since they invoked God as the Prophet's Lord.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r7.anchor: وعندي أن الظاهر أن ذلك القول بأي معنى كان صادر على سبيل التهكم إذا كان المراد بالرب

ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r8.speaker: عروة بن الزبير، هشام، أبو حيوة، أبو بحرية، ابن أبي عبلة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r8.claim: They read ما ودعك with a lightened dāl; Ibn Jinnī says this was the Prophet's reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ عروة بن الزبير وابنه هشام وأبو حيوة وأبو بحرية وابن أبي عبلة ما ودعك بالتخفيف

ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r9.claim: The lightened reading is explained as a reduced form of ودع, or as the original verb meaning left, though the latter challenges grammarians' claim that Arabs abandoned it.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r9.anchor: وخرجت على أن ودع مخفف ودع ومعناه معناه قال في القاموس ودعه كوضعه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r10.speaker: المغرب
ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r10.claim: It says grammarians claimed the past verb and its derivatives were obsolete, but the Prophet used ودع in a hadith about abandoning congregational prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p155#2/r10.anchor: وفي المغرب أن النحاة زعموا أن العرب أماتت ذلك والنبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم أفصحهم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r1.claim: Abū al-Aswad's poem and another poet's verse attest actual Arabic use of ودع as a verb of leaving, including with two objects.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r1.anchor: غاله في الحب حتى ودعه ومثله قول آخر وثم ودعنا آل عمرو

ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r2.claim: A prophetic saying about leaving the Turks and Abyssinians is also cited as usage evidence.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r2.anchor: وفي الحديث اتركوا الترك ما تركوكم ودعوا الحبشة ما ودعوكم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r3.speaker: المستوفي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r3.claim: He says these forms occur in Arabic and grammar authorities do not overrule usage, although the forms are rare.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r3.anchor: وفي المستوفي أن كل ذلك قد ورد في كلام العرب ولا عبرة بكلام النحاة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r4.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r4.claim: Al-Tibi says the reading's parallel wording and rhyme-like arrangement offset its rarity; another view says it echoes the mockers' own unusual wording.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r4.anchor: وقال الطيبي بعد أن ذكر وروده نظما ونثرا إنما حسن هذه القراءة الموافقة بين الكلمتين

ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r5.claim: Once the lightened form is shown to be attested, no contrived rhetorical defense of it is needed.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r5.anchor: والحق أنه بعد ثبوت وروده لا يحتاج إلى تكليف محسن له

ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r6.claim: Here رب is God; calling Him the Prophet's Lord conveys tenderness as the one who nurtures and gradually brings him to his fitting perfection.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r6.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد بالرب هو الله عز وجل وفي التعبير عنه بعنوان الربوبية وإضافته إلى ضميره

ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r7.claim: Qalā means to hate, and its object is omitted to avoid confronting the Prophet with the word or to deny hatred toward him and his followers.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r7.anchor: وما قلى أي وما أبغضك وحذف المفعول لئلا يواجه عليه الصلاة والسلام بنسبة القلي

ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r8.claim: The object may instead be omitted because it was already mentioned, for economy, and to preserve the verse endings.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r8.anchor: أو للأستغناء عنه بذكره من قبل مع أن فيه مراعاة للفواصل

ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r9.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r9.claim: He defines qalā as intense hatred and derives it either from throwing away or from roasting, depending on whether the root is wāw or yāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r9.anchor: وفي مفردات الراغب القلي شدة البغض يقال قلاه يقلوه ويقليه فمن جعله من الواوي

ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r10.speaker: المفسرون
ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r10.claim: Commentators say Gabriel was delayed, prompting the polytheists to claim that the Prophet's Lord had hated and abandoned him.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r10.anchor: قال المفسرون أبطأ جبريل عليه السلام على النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم فقال

ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r11.speaker: زيد بن أرقم
ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r11.claim: A report says Umm Jamīl taunted the Prophet after revelation paused, claiming that his Lord had abandoned and hated him; the verse then came down.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r11.anchor: عن زيد ابن أرقم قال لما نزلت تبت يدا أبي لهب

ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r12.speaker: جندب البجلي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r12.claim: Tirmidhī, who authenticates the report, relates that after the Prophet injured a finger and paused night prayer for two or three nights, a woman said his devil had left him.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p156/r12.anchor: أخرج الترمذي وصححه وابن أبي حاتم واللفظ له عن جندب البجلي قال رمى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p157/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157/r1.claim: The Jundub report continues: after the Prophet recited that he was a wounded finger in the path of God, he did not rise for two or three nights and a woman blamed his devil.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157/r1.anchor: ما أنت إلا اصبع دميت وفي سبيل الله ما لقيت فمكث ليلتين أو ثلاثا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p157/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157/r2.claim: Other Tirmidhī, Aḥmad, Bukhārī, Muslim, and Nasāʾī versions say the Prophet was ill and did not rise for two or three nights; they omit the woman and injury without undermining the report.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157/r2.anchor: وفي رواية للترمذي أيضا والإمام أحمد والبخاري ومسلم والنسائي وجماعة بلفظ اشتكى النبي

ALUSI-FULL:v30p157/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157/r3.speaker: المفسرون
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157/r3.claim: Another occasion says Jews asked about the Sleepers, the Spirit, and Dhū al-Qarnayn; the Prophet promised an answer the next day without saying if God wills, then revelation paused and mockers spoke.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157/r3.anchor: وقال جمع من المفسرسن أن اليهود سألوه عليه الصلاة والسلام عن أصحاب الكهف وعن الروح وعن قصة ذي القرنين

ALUSI-FULL:v30p157/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157/r4.claim: A report says Uthmān gave grapes or dates to the Prophet, who repeatedly gave them to a requester; revelation then paused for days and the Prophet felt unsettled.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157/r4.anchor: وقيل إن عثمان أهدى إليه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عنقود عنب وقيل عذق تمر

ALUSI-FULL:v30p157/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157/r5.speaker: خولة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157/r5.claim: Khawla reports that a dead puppy under the Prophet's bed kept Gabriel away for four days until she found and removed it, after which the revelation resumed.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157/r5.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة في مسنده والطبراني وابن مردويه من حديث خولة وكانت تخدم رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v30p157/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157/r6.speaker: ابن جريج، الكلبي، ابن عباس، السدي ومقاتل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157/r6.claim: Reports give different durations for the revelation's pause: twelve, fifteen, several, twenty-five, or forty days; the author says the starting point is hard to determine precisely.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157/r6.anchor: وعن ابن جريج أنه كان اثني عشر يوما وعن الكلبي خمسة عشر يوما وقيل بضعة عشر يوما

ALUSI-FULL:v30p157#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157#2/r1.claim: The continuation recounts a report that the Prophet told Khadīja his Lord had abandoned and hated him after revelation paused.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157#2/r1.anchor: ابطأ الوحي على رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم فقال لخديجة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p157#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157#2/r2.claim: The report troubles the author because the Prophet could not think God had removed him from prophethood, and knew revelation's delay and return served wisdom.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157#2/r2.anchor: هذا بأنه لا يليق بالرسول صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم أن يظن أن الله تعالى شأنه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p157#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157#2/r3.claim: Proposed defenses say the Prophet was testing Khadīja, exposing the mockers' claim, or describing the delay as resembling abandonment; the author calls the report anomalous and unreliable.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157#2/r3.anchor: وأجيب بأن مراده عليه الصلاة والسلام إن صح أن يجربها ليعرف قدر علمها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p157#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157#2/r4.speaker: عروة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157#2/r4.claim: Another report says Khadīja inferred that God had hated the Prophet from his distress during Gabriel's delay; the author calls this implausible.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157#2/r4.anchor: ونحوها ما دل على أن قائل ذاك خديجة رضي الله تعالى عنها أخرج ابن جرير وابن المنذر عن عروة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p157#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157#2/r5.claim: The sound reports relied on by most say the polytheists made the taunt, while the Prophet grieved naturally over their words and his separation from Gabriel.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157#2/r5.anchor: والمعول ما عليه الجمهور وصحت به الأخبار أن القائل هم المشركون وأنه عليه الصلاة والسلام

ALUSI-FULL:v30p157#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157#2/r6.claim: One report says the Prophet told Gabriel he had missed him, and Gabriel replied that he had missed the Prophet even more but was commanded; he recited that descent is only by God's command.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157#2/r6.anchor: وفي بعض الآثار أنه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قال لجبريل عليه السلام ما جئتني حتى اشتقت إليك

ALUSI-FULL:v30p157#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157#2/r7.claim: Another version says Gabriel explained that angels do not enter a house containing a dog or an image; the author allows that several causes may have contributed to the delay.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157#2/r7.anchor: وفي رواية أنه عاتبه عليهما الصلاة والسلام فقال أما علمت أنا لا ندخل بيتا فيه كلب ولا صورة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p157#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157#2/r8.claim: The author dismisses a proposal that ربك here means Gabriel as the Prophet's companion rather than God.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157#2/r8.anchor: ثم أنه قد زعم بعض بناء على بعض الروايات السابقة جواز أن يكون المراد بربك

ALUSI-FULL:v30p157#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157#2/r9.claim: Since the verse denies abandonment and hatred in this life, it reassures the Prophet that the blessings awaiting him in the afterlife are greater.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p157#2/r9.anchor: وحيث تضمن ما سبق من نفي التوديع والقلي أنه عز وجل لا يزال يواصله عليه الصلاة والسلام بالوحي

BAGHAWI:93:1/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:93:1/r2.speaker: جندب بن سفيان
BAGHAWI:93:1/r2.claim: Jundub ibn Sufyan reports that after the Prophet was ill and did not rise for two or three nights, a woman taunted him that his Satan had left; then the opening verses were revealed.
BAGHAWI:93:1/r2.anchor: سمعت جندب بن سفيان قال : " اشتكى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAGHAWI:93:1/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:93:1/r3.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI:93:1/r3.claim: Another report identifies the woman who taunted the Prophet as Umm Jamil, the wife of Abu Lahab.
BAGHAWI:93:1/r3.anchor: وقيل : إن المرأة التي قالت ذلك أم جميل امرأة أبي لهب

BAGHAWI:93:1/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:93:1/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:93:1/r7.claim: When polytheists said God had abandoned and hated Muhammad, the surah was revealed; the Prophet said he missed Gabriel, who replied that he too yearned but was only a commanded servant.
BAGHAWI:93:1/r7.anchor: فقال المشركون : إن محمداً ودعه ربه وقلاه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p450/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p450/r1.speaker: جندب بن سفيان
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p450/r1.claim: Jundub reports that after the Prophet was ill and missed two or three nights of prayer, a woman said his devil had left him; the verses were then revealed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p450/r1.anchor: اشتكى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فلم يقم ليلتين أو ثلاثا فجاءت امرأة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p450/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p450/r2.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p450/r2.claim: An alternative report identifies the woman who taunted the Prophet as Umm Jamil, the wife of Abu Lahab.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p450/r2.anchor: إن المرأة التي قالت ذلك أم جميل امرأة أبي لهب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p450/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p450/r3.speaker: المفسرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p450/r3.claim: The commentators say Jews asked about Dhul-Qarnayn, the People of the Cave, and the Spirit; the Prophet promised an answer the next day without saying if God wills, so revelation paused.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p450/r3.anchor: سألت اليهود، رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن ذي القرنين وأصحاب الكهف وعن الروح؟

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p450/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p450/r4.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p450/r4.claim: Zayd says Gabriel's delay was caused by a puppy in the Prophet's house; Gabriel explained that angels do not enter a house with a dog or image.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p450/r4.anchor: كان سبب احتباس جبريل عليه السلام عنه كون جرو في بيته

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p450/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p450/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p450/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj gives the duration of the pause in revelation as twelve days.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p450/r5.anchor: فقال ابن جريج: اثنا عشر يوما.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p450/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p450/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p450/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas gives the duration of the pause in revelation as fifteen days.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p450/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: خمسة عشر يوما.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p450/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p450/r7.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p450/r7.claim: Maqatil gives the duration of the pause in revelation as forty days.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p450/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p450/r8.speaker: المشركون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p450/r8.claim: When the polytheists said Muhammad's Lord had abandoned and disliked him, God revealed this sura.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p450/r8.anchor: فقال المشركون: إن محمدا ودعه ربه وقلاه، فأنزل الله تعالى هذه السورة،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p450/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p450/r9.speaker: جبريل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p450/r9.claim: After the pause, the Prophet said he had missed Gabriel; Gabriel said he missed him even more but was an appointed servant, and the source links this to God's command governing revelation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p450/r9.anchor: فقال جبريل: "إني كنت أشد شوقا [إليك] (1) ، وكلني عبد مأمور"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p454/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p454/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p454/r10.claim: The oath's answer assures the Prophet that his Lord has neither left him since choosing him nor hated him since loving him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p454/r10.anchor: هذا جواب القسم، أي ما تركك منذ اختارك ولا أبغضك منذ أحبك.

BAYDAWI-FULL:93:1-3/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:1-3/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:1-3/r3.claim: God has neither abandoned nor hated the Prophet; the omitted object of قلى is understood from the prior mention and suits the rhyme, and lighter ودع has the sense ‘left.’
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:1-3/r3.anchor: { ما ودعك ربك } ما قطعك قطع المودع، وقرىء بالتخفيف بمعنى ما تركك

BAYDAWI-FULL:93:1-3/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:1-3/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:1-3/r4.claim: The revelation paused for days because the Prophet omitted ‘if God wills,’ rebuked a persistent questioner, a dead puppy lay under his bed, or another reason; polytheists said God had abandoned and hated him, prompting this response.
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:1-3/r4.anchor: روي أن الوحي تأخر عنه أياما لتركه الاستثناء كما مر في سورة «الكهف»

BINTSHATI:v1p23/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p23/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p23/r1.claim: The surah is Meccan without disagreement and is commonly placed eleventh in revelation order, after al-Fajr.
BINTSHATI:v1p23/r1.anchor: السورة مكية بلا خلاف، والمشهور أنها الحادية عشرة في ترتيب النزول. نزلت بعد الفجر

BINTSHATI:v1p23/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p23/r2.speaker: المفسرون
BINTSHATI:v1p23/r2.claim: Commentators agree that the occasion was the early delay of revelation, which distressed the Prophet.
BINTSHATI:v1p23/r2.anchor: المفسرون مجمعون على أن سبب النزول، هو إبطاء الوحي في أوائله على الرسول

BINTSHATI:v1p23/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p23/r3.speaker: رسول الله
BINTSHATI:v1p23/r3.claim: One report says the Prophet told Khadija that his Lord had forsaken and hated him; she reassured him and the verse came down.
BINTSHATI:v1p23/r3.anchor: ففي رواية أنه رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -، وقد شكا إلى زوجة السيدة خديجة

BINTSHATI:v1p23/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p23/r4.speaker: السيدة خديجة
BINTSHATI:v1p23/r4.claim: A second report makes Khadija the speaker who was troubled by the pause in revelation.
BINTSHATI:v1p23/r4.anchor: وفي راوية ثانية، أنها السيدة خديجة، وقد رابها فتور الوحي

BINTSHATI:v1p23/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p23/r5.speaker: أم جميلة امرأة أبي لهب
BINTSHATI:v1p23/r5.claim: A third report says Umm Jamil taunted Muhammad that his demon had abandoned him.
BINTSHATI:v1p23/r5.anchor: هي التي قالت: يا محمد! ما أرى شيطانك إلا قد تركك

BINTSHATI:v1p23/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p23/r6.speaker: المشركون
BINTSHATI:v1p23/r6.claim: A fourth report says the polytheists gloated that Muhammad's Lord had abandoned and hated him.
BINTSHATI:v1p23/r6.anchor: ورواية رابعة تقول: إن المشركين هم الذين قالوا في شماتة

BINTSHATI:v1p23/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p23/r7.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p23/r7.claim: Reports of occasions are contextual clues, not necessarily causal legal explanations; early authorities admit uncertainty and disagreement, and the verses came down around the event.
BINTSHATI:v1p23/r7.anchor: أسباب النزول لا تعدو أ، تكون قرائن مما حول النص، وهي بإعتراف الأقدمين أنفسهم لا تخلو من وهم

BINTSHATI:v1p26/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p26/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p26/r1.claim: The daily alternation from bright duha to a quiet night is a sensory image that prepares for the unseen pause in revelation, without suggesting that heaven abandoned earth.
BINTSHATI:v1p26/r1.anchor: تألق الضوء في ضحوة النهار، ثم فتور الليل إذا سجا وسكن

BINTSHATI:v1p26/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p26/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p26/r2.claim: The sensory contrast between light and darkness can clarify unseen guidance and truth or misguidance and falsehood.
BINTSHATI:v1p26/r2.anchor: معاني من الهدى والحق، أو الضلال والباطل، بماديات من النور والظلمة

BINTSHATI:v1p27/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p27/r1.speaker: فخر الدين الرازي ونظام الدين النيسابوري
BINTSHATI:v1p27/r1.claim: They also say the oath answers the disbelievers' taunt: they were unable to prove their claim that God had abandoned Muhammad.
BINTSHATI:v1p27/r1.anchor: هاتوا الحجة، فعجزوا، فلزمه اليمين بأنه ما ودعه ربه ما قلاه

BINTSHATI:v1p27/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p27/r3.speaker: الشيخ محمد عبده
BINTSHATI:v1p27/r3.claim: Abduh says the Prophet's distress during the pause was relieved by renewed revelation: duha represents life-giving first revelation, while quiet night restores strength for later work.
BINTSHATI:v1p27/r3.anchor: فآتاه الله ما كان في شوق إليه، وثبته بالوحي وبشره أن تلك الفترة لم تكن عن ترك ولا عن قلى

BINTSHATI:v1p27/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p27/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p27/r4.claim: The author's sensory analogy is nearly lost in Abduh's account of night as rest and preparation for work.
BINTSHATI:v1p27/r4.anchor: ويوشك الملحظ البيلني، أن يتوه وسط هذا الكلام في الضحى تقوى به الحياة

BINTSHATI:v1p27/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p27/r5.speaker: ابن قيم الجوزية
BINTSHATI:v1p27/r5.claim: Ibn al-Qayyim comes close to matching the bright duha after darkness with revelation after its pause, but frames the oath as proof of God's lordship, wisdom, and mercy.
BINTSHATI:v1p27/r5.anchor: وكان "إبن قيم الجوزية" أقرب إلى إدراك الملحظ البياني

BINTSHATI:v1p28/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p28/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p28/r1.claim: The author says Ibn al-Qayyim's appeal to doubts about God's lordship misses the stated occasion, which concerns a claim that God abandoned Muhammad.
BINTSHATI:v1p28/r1.anchor: الموقف كان ارتياباً من المشركين في ربوبية الله وحكمته ورحمته، وإنما كان - على قول المفسرين في سبب النزول - كلاماً

BINTSHATI:v1p28/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p28/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p28/r3.claim: The author finds no clear connection between the oath and its answer in the accounts of al-Tabari, al-Zamakhshari, and Abu Hayyan, and notes they do not compare it with God's explicit denials of oaths.
BINTSHATI:v1p28/r3.anchor: لم يتعرض "إبن جرير الطبري" لبيان ارتباط المقسم به

BINTSHATI:v1p32/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p32/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p32/r2.claim: The author excludes esoteric readings that turn duha and night into the Prophet's face and hair, male and female relatives, knowledge and forgiveness, or Islam's rise and later estrangement.
BINTSHATI:v1p32/r2.anchor: ولا نقف بعد هذا عند تأويلات الإشاريين بأن الضحى وجه محمد، - صلى الله عليه وسلم - والليل شعره

BINTSHATI:v1p32/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p32/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p32/r3.claim: The majority read wadda'aka with a doubled dāl, while some read the verb with a light dāl; eloquent Arabic generally avoided the simple triliteral form.
BINTSHATI:v1p32/r3.anchor: والقراءة بالدال المشددة هي قراءة الجمهور، وقرأ بعضهم:

BINTSHATI:v1p32/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p32/r4.speaker: الزمخشري والجوهري
BINTSHATI:v1p32/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari cites poetry using wada'a, while al-Jawhari says such usage may be confined to poetic necessity; Khifaf uses mawdu' to mean left.
BINTSHATI:v1p32/r4.anchor: ولكن الجوهري في (الصحاح) صرح بأن مثل هذا ربما جاء

BINTSHATI:v1p33/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p33/r1.speaker: أبو حيان
BINTSHATI:v1p33/r1.claim: Abu Hayyan says eloquent Arabic dispensed with the simple triliteral form, and a lexicon commentator's objection does not undo that point.
BINTSHATI:v1p33/r1.anchor: لا تدفع ما قاله: أبو حيان

BINTSHATI:v1p33/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p33/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI:v1p33/r2.claim: Wada' means leaving, with tawdi' intensifying the sense because a person who bids farewell leaves you emphatically.

BINTSHATI:v1p33/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p33/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p33/r3.claim: The root occurs elsewhere in Qur'anic imperative and mustawda' forms, while 93:3 is its only past-tense verb use.
BINTSHATI:v1p33/r3.anchor: ولم يجيء من المادة في القرآن، بصيغة الفعل الماضي إلا آية الضحى

BINTSHATI:v1p33/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p33/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p33/r4.claim: Qala means intense hatred; its sensory root may suggest agitation, which extends to withdrawal and departure, and Ibn Sida defines it as utmost hatred followed by leaving.
BINTSHATI:v1p33/r4.anchor: قليته قلى أبغضته وكرهته غاية الكره فتركته

BINTSHATI:v1p34/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p34/r1.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI:v1p34/r1.claim: Al-Raghib glosses qala in both Qur'anic occurrences as intense hatred and aversion.

BINTSHATI:v1p34/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p34/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI:v1p34/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the omitted object of qala is obvious and shortened, comparing the omission to another Qur'anic construction.

BINTSHATI:v1p34/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p34/r3.speaker: الطبري وأبو حيان
BINTSHATI:v1p34/r3.claim: Al-Tabari and Abu Hayyan explain the omitted addressee through the preceding mention of the Prophet and as concise expression.
BINTSHATI:v1p34/r3.anchor: إنه اكتفاء بفهم السامع لمعناه، إذ كان قد تقدم ذلك قوله: ما ودعك

BINTSHATI:v1p34/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p34/r4.speaker: النيسابوري
BINTSHATI:v1p34/r4.claim: Al-Nisaburi adds that omission preserves the rhyme endings of the surah.

BINTSHATI:v1p34/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p34/r5.speaker: الرازي
BINTSHATI:v1p34/r5.claim: Al-Razi gives three reasons: the earlier kaaf suffices, rhyme requires omission, or the unrestricted object includes all who love the Prophet; the author rejects the expansive reading as unsupported by context.
BINTSHATI:v1p34/r5.anchor: فائدة الإطلاق، أي أنه ما قلاك ولا أحداً من أصحابك

BINTSHATI:v1p35/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p35/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p35/r1.claim: The author rejects rhyme alone as the reason for omission: the Qur'anic style is not governed by form alone, and the surah's last verse does not follow a th-rhyme or use a substitute verb to force one.
BINTSHATI:v1p35/r1.anchor: ليس من المقبول عندنا أن يقوم البيان القرآني على اعتبار لفظي محض

BINTSHATI:v1p35/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p35/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p35/r2.claim: The addressee is clear from what precedes; omitting the harsh verb comforts the Prophet, since qala implies expulsion and severe hatred, while tawdi' can suggest reluctant parting and hoped-for return.
BINTSHATI:v1p35/r2.anchor: تحاشي خطابه تعالى لحبيبه المصطفى في مقام الإيناس: ما قلاك

BINTSHATI:v1p35/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p35/r3.speaker: الرازي والنيسابوري
BINTSHATI:v1p35/r3.claim: Some explain the delay by the Prophet's failure to say God willing after promising answers to Jewish questions, or by a puppy or untrimmed nails preventing Gabriel's entry; the author rejects these as strained, and notes the puppy story conflicts with the children's post-Hijra birth.
BINTSHATI:v1p35/r3.anchor: أن اليهود سألوا النبي عن ثلاث نسائل: الروح، وذي القرنين واصحاب الكهف

BIQAI-FULL:v8p453/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p453/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p453/r1.claim: God did not leave the Prophet in a separation like that of a departing person; God is his Lord who created, perfected, and nurtured him.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p453/r1.anchor: ما ودعك } أي تركك تركا يحصل به فرقة كفرقة المودع

BIQAI-FULL:v8p453/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p453/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p453/r2.claim: The verb qalaa denies hatred as well as abandonment; omitting its object shortens the wording while widening the meaning.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p453/r2.anchor: وما قلى * } أي وما أبغضك بغضا ما , وحذف الضمير اختصارا لفظيا ليعم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p453/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p453/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p453/r3.claim: The verses were revealed after revelation paused: the Prophet had promised answers about the Spirit, the Cave Companions, and Dhū al-Qarnayn without saying “if God wills,” prompting claims that his Lord had forsaken him.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p453/r3.anchor: سألوه عن الروح وقصة أهل الكهف وذي القرنين

BIQAI-FULL:v8p453/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p453/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p453/r4.claim: When the verses came, the Prophet said takbīr; the author says takbīr became a practice in this surah and those that follow.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p453/r4.anchor: ولما نزلت كبر صلى الله عليه وسلم فكان التكبير فيها وفيما بعدها سنة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p453/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p453/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p453/r5.claim: The passage distinguishes four relations: obedient believers are near and loved, unbelievers distant and hated, sinful believers mixed, and unbelievers’ outward worship has no acceptance.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p453/r5.anchor: وقد أفهمت هذه العبارة أن المراتب التقريبية أربع

BIQAI-FULL:v8p453/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p453/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v8p453/r6.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says the predestination discussion could cause fear, so God reassured His dearest servant by recounting his favor and the good of both lives.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p453/r6.anchor: أنس تعالى أحب عباده إليه وأعظمهم منزلة لديه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r1.claim: The blessings recall the Prophet’s mercy and gentleness toward believers, as described in the cited verses.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r1.anchor: عزيز عليه ما عنتم حريص عليكم بالمؤمنين رؤوف رحيم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r3.claim: Some servants gain clear insight through steadfast piety and reflection, moving from inference to direct recognition of the path.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r3.anchor: بل قد يطلع سبحانه خواص عباده - بملازمته التقوى والاعتبار - على واضحة السبيل

BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r4.speaker: النبي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r4.claim: The Prophet told Ḥāritha, and similarly Abū Bakr, that he had found the truth and should remain firm in it.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r4.anchor: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لحارثة : ( وجدت فالزم ) وقال مثله للصديق

BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r5.claim: The faithful receive good news in both lives and angelic reassurance, walking by a light God grants them.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r5.anchor: لهم البشرى في الحياة الدنيا وفي الآخرة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r6.claim: The surah’s consolation is linked to promises of angels’ protection and God-given light and discernment.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r7.claim: The author compares guided believers to someone brought from death into light, unlike one trapped in darkness.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r7.anchor: أو من كان ميتا فأحييناه وجعلنا له نورا يمشي به

BIQAI-FULL:v8p455/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p455/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p455/r2.claim: The many human paths reduce to belief or disbelief and to Paradise or Hell, as paired creation and flight toward God indicate.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p455/r2.anchor: ولانحصار السبل وإن تشعبت في طريقي

NAHHAS:v5p249/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p249/r2.speaker: الضحاك
NAHHAS:v5p249/r2.claim: He paraphrases the clause as ‘He did not hate you.’

NAHHAS:v5p249/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p249/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p249/r3.claim: Arabic may omit the second verb when the first supplies it, as in ‘I gave you and honored [you].’
NAHHAS:v5p249/r3.anchor: العرب تحذف من الثاني لدلالة الأولى يقال أعطيتك وأكرمت

NAHHAS:v5p249/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p249/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v5p249/r4.claim: He glosses the phrase as God neither abandoning nor hating the Prophet.
NAHHAS:v5p249/r4.anchor: وروى ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس ما ودعك ربك وما قلى قال يقول ما تركك وما أبغضك

NAHHAS:v5p249/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p249/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
NAHHAS:v5p249/r5.claim: He records the shortened form waddaʿaka.

NAHHAS:v5p249/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p249/r6.speaker: سيبويه
NAHHAS:v5p249/r6.claim: He disallows the verb wadaʿa because speakers replaced it with taraka.
NAHHAS:v5p249/r6.anchor: ومنع سيبويه أن يقال ودع قال استغنوا عنه بترك

NAHHAS:v5p249/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p249/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p249/r7.claim: Another explanation is that Arabs find initial wāw heavy; the sister letter yāʾ can occur there, and forms like diminutive and plural wāṣil begin with hamza.
NAHHAS:v5p249/r7.anchor: والعلة عند غيره أن العرب تستثقل الواو في أول الكلمة لثقلها يدل على ذلك أنها لا توجد زائدة في أول الكلام وتوجد أختها الياء نحو يعملة ويربوع وأنك إذا صغرت واصلا قلت أو يصل لا غير وفي الجمع أواصل

NAHHAS:v5p249/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p249/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p249/r8.claim: Qalā yaqlī or yaqlā means to hate.
NAHHAS:v5p249/r8.anchor: ويقال قلاه يقليه إذا أبغضه ويقال أيضا يقلاه

DURR-FULL:v8p539/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p539/r4.speaker: جندب البجلي
DURR-FULL:v8p539/r4.claim: When the Prophet was ill and did not rise at night for two or three nights, a woman taunted him that his devil had abandoned him; the opening verses answered her.
DURR-FULL:v8p539/r4.anchor: والنسائي وابن جرير والطبراني والبيهقي وأبو نعيم معا في الدلائل عن جندب البجلي

DURR-FULL:v8p539/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p539/r5.speaker: جندب
DURR-FULL:v8p539/r5.claim: When Gabriel was delayed, polytheists said Muhammad had been abandoned; the verse denied that God had left him.
DURR-FULL:v8p539/r5.anchor: وأخرج الفريابي وسعيد بن منصور وعبد بن حميد وابن جرير وابن المنذر والطبراني وابن مردويه عن جندب

DURR-FULL:v8p539/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p539/r6.speaker: جندب
DURR-FULL:v8p539/r6.claim: When Gabriel was withheld, a cousin's daughter said the Prophet's companion had left him; the passage was revealed.

DURR-FULL:v8p539/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p539/r7.speaker: جندب
DURR-FULL:v8p539/r7.claim: After a stone injured his finger and the Prophet stopped night prayer for two or three nights, a woman blamed his devil's departure; al-Tirmidhi authenticated the report.
DURR-FULL:v8p539/r7.anchor: وأخرج الترمذي وصححه وابن أبي حاتم واللفظ له عن جندب

DURR-FULL:v8p540/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p540/r1.speaker: زيد بن أرقم
DURR-FULL:v8p540/r1.claim: After Abu Lahab's surah, his wife confronted the Prophet; when revelation paused and she said his companion had abandoned and hated him, the opening verses were revealed.
DURR-FULL:v8p540/r1.anchor: وأخرج الحاكم عن زيد بن أرقم

DURR-FULL:v8p540/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p540/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن شداد
DURR-FULL:v8p540/r2.claim: He reports Khadija saying that the Prophet's Lord seemed to have rejected him, after which the verses were revealed.
DURR-FULL:v8p540/r2.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن عبد الله بن شداد

DURR-FULL:v8p540/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p540/r3.speaker: عروة
DURR-FULL:v8p540/r3.claim: When Gabriel was delayed and the Prophet became distressed, Khadija inferred from his distress that God had rejected him; the surah followed.
DURR-FULL:v8p540/r3.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير وابن المنذر عن عروة

DURR-FULL:v8p540/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p540/r4.speaker: خديجة
DURR-FULL:v8p540/r4.claim: In another report, she told the distressed Prophet that God seemed to have rejected him while revelation was delayed; the verse denied this.
DURR-FULL:v8p540/r4.anchor: وأخرج الحاكم وابن مردويه والبيهقي في الدلائل من طريق عروة عن خديجة

DURR-FULL:v8p540/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p540/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p540/r5.claim: After revelation paused for days, polytheists taunted that God had abandoned Muhammad; the passage came down, and the night ‘when it settles’ means when it arrives.
DURR-FULL:v8p540/r5.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير وابن مردويه من طريق العوفي عن ابن عباس

DURR-FULL:v8p540/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p540/r6.speaker: قتادة والضحاك
DURR-FULL:v8p540/r6.claim: Their mursal reports give the same occasion: a pause in revelation prompted the claim that God had abandoned Muhammad, answered by this passage.
DURR-FULL:v8p540/r6.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير نحوه من مرسل قتادة والضحاك

DURR-FULL:v8p541/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p541/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p541/r5.claim: In another report the night has departed; God has neither left nor hated the Prophet.
DURR-FULL:v8p541/r5.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير وابن أبي حاتم وابن المنذر مردويه عن ابن عباس

DURR-FULL:v8p541/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p541/r6.speaker: أم حفص
DURR-FULL:v8p541/r6.claim: A dead puppy hidden beneath the Prophet's bed delayed revelation for four days; after Khawla found it, the Prophet trembled and the passage through ‘you will be satisfied’ came down.
DURR-FULL:v8p541/r6.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة في مسنده والطبراني وابن مردويه عن أم حفص عن أمها

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3442/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3442/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3442/r1.claim: Jundub reports that after the Prophet missed night prayer for one or two nights, a woman taunted him that his devil had left; the sura was revealed to reassure him that God had neither abandoned nor hated him.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3442/r1.anchor: عن الاسود بن قيس قال : سمعت جندبا يقول : اشتكى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3442/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3442/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3442/r2.claim: A second Jundub report says a stone injured the Prophet's finger; after two or three nights without rising, a woman said his devil had left, and the same verses were revealed.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3442/r2.anchor: حدثني الاسود بن قيس ، انه سمع جندبا يقول : رمى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بحجر في اصبعه

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3442#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3442#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3442#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses God's not leaving the Prophet as not abandoning him, and God's not hating him as not despising him.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3442#2/r3.anchor: ما ودعك ربك قال : ما تركك وما قلى قال : ما ابغضك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p394#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p394#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p394#2/r1.claim: The oath rebuts the idolaters' claim that revelation stopped when the Prophet did not recite the Quran at night for several days; the warning targets their insinuation, since the Prophet himself had no doubt.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p394#2/r1.anchor: القسم لتأكيد الخبر ردا على زعم المشركين أن الوحي انقطع عن النبي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p394#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p394#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p394#2/r6.claim: The denial of abandonment answers the oath; a negative oath response is not prefixed with لام.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p394#2/r6.anchor: وجملة : { ما ودعك ربك } الخ جواب القسم ، وجواب القسم إذا كان جملة منفية لم تقترن باللام .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p395/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p395/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p395/r1.claim: Farewell is a traveler's greeting; here it metaphorically means separation after connection, comparing interrupted speech to departure, although the attribution is only figurative because God has no ordinary human contact with people. It denies that God stopped revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p395/r1.anchor: والتوديع : تحية من يريد السفر . واستعير في الآية للمفارقة بعد الاتصال تشبيها بفراق المسافر في انقطاع الصلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p395/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p395/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p395/r2.claim: The added denial of hatred rejects both mockeries: some said the Lord had left the Prophet and others said He hated him; the coordinated clause shares the oath-response syntax.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p395/r2.anchor: وقد عطف عليه : { وما قلى } للإتيان على إبطال مقالتي المشركين إذ قال بعضهم : ودعه ربه ، وقال بعضهم : قلاه ربه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p395/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p395/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p395/r3.claim: قلي and قلى, with the stated alternative vowels, mean intense hatred; the surah's opening explains the setting of the idolaters' remarks.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p395/r3.anchor: والقلي ( بفتح القاف مع سكون اللام ) والقلى ( بكسر القاف مع فتح اللام ) : البغض الشديد ، وسبب مقالة المشركين تقدم في صدر السورة .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p395/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p395/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جريج
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p395/r4.claim: They report a second interruption of revelation lasting about fifteen days, after which idolaters said Muhammad's Lord had abandoned and hated him, prompting the verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p395/r4.anchor: فعن ابن عباس وابن جريج : ( احتبس الوحي عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خمسة عشر يوما أو نحوها . فقال المشركون : إن محمدا ودعه ربه وقلاه ، فنزلت الآية ) .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p395/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p395/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p395/r5.claim: Revelation paused twice: first before al-Mudaththir or al-Muzzammil, after two or three surahs, when the Prophet feared revelation had ended and then saw Gabriel on a chair between heaven and earth; this early pause, perhaps forty days, went unnoticed by idolaters.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p395/r5.anchor: واحتباس الوحي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقع مرتين : أولاهما : قبل نزول سورة المدثر أو المزمل ، أي بعد نزول سورتين من القرآن أو ثلاث على الخلاف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p395/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p395/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p395/r6.claim: The second pause followed roughly eight more surahs, making this the eleventh in revelation order, consistent with its chronological placement.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p395/r6.anchor: وبذلك تكون هذه السورة حادية عشرة فيتوافق ذلك مع عددها في ترتيب نزول السور .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r5.speaker: جمهور القراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r5.claim: Most readers pronounce waddaʿaka with a doubled dal, from farewell.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس «ودعك» بشد الدال من التوديع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r6.speaker: عروة بن الزبير وابنه هشام
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r6.claim: Urwa ibn al-Zubayr and his son Hisham read an undoubled form meaning he left you.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ عروة بن الزبير وابنه هشام «ودعك» بتخفيف الدال بمعنى ترك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r8.claim: A report says revelation paused for a disputed period in Mecca, distressing the Prophet, and Umm Jamil said his devil had abandoned him; the verse answered her.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r8.anchor: فقال ابن عباس وغيره: أبطأ الوحي مرة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو بمكة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r9.speaker: عروة بن الزبير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r9.claim: Urwa reports that Khadija said God had left the Prophet because he grieved excessively over delayed revelation; the verse answered her.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r9.anchor: وقال ابن وهب عن رجال عن عروة بن الزبير أن خديجة قالت له

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r10.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r10.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says Gabriel was delayed because a puppy was in the Prophet's house.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r10.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم: إنما احتبس عنه جبريل لجرو كلب كان في بيته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p157/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p157/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب وأنس وعروة وأبو العالية وابن يعمر وابن أبي عبلة وأبو حاتم عن يعقوب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p157/r1.claim: They read waddaʿaka with a light, undoubled dāl.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p157/r1.anchor: وقرأ عمر بن الخطاب وأنس وعروة وأبو العالية وابن يعمر وابن أبي عبلة وأبو حاتم عن يعقوب ما ودعك بتخفيف الدال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p157/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p157/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p157/r2.claim: The oath's answer says God did not bid the Prophet farewell like someone departing, and did not hate him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p157/r2.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة ما ودعك من التوديع كما يودع المفارق و ما ودعك مخففة من ودعه يدعه وما قلى أي أبغض

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p424/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p424/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p424/r1.claim: After the Prophet did not rise for one or two nights while ill, a woman accused his devil of abandoning him; the Prophet's report says the opening verses were then revealed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p424/r1.anchor: فقالت: يا محمد، ما أرى شيطانك إلا قد تركك.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p424/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p424/r2.speaker: مشركون
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p424/r2.claim: In another version, Gabriel's delay led the polytheists to say Muhammad had been abandoned, and the verses were revealed in response.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p424/r2.anchor: قال: أبطأ جبريل على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فقال المشركون: ودع محمد.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p424/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p424/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p424/r3.claim: Another narration says a stone injured the Prophet's finger, after which he stopped night worship for two or three nights and a woman made the same accusation; Ibn Kathir calls the injury report authentic but the causal link unusual.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p424/r3.anchor: رمي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بحجر في أصبعه فقال:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p424/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p424/r4.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p424/r4.claim: Ibn Ishaq says the woman who made the accusation was Umm Jamil, the wife of Abu Lahab.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p424/r4.anchor: قيل: إن هذه المرأة هي: أم جميل امرأة أبي لهب،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p424/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p424/r5.speaker: خديجة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p424/r5.claim: Ibn Jarir reports that Khadijah told the Prophet she thought his Lord had rejected him, after which the opening verses were revealed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p424/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله ابن شداد: أن خديجة قالت للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: ما أرى ربك إلا قد قلاك.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says revelation paused for several days, distressing the Prophet; the polytheists said his Lord had abandoned and hated him, and the verse answered them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425/r1.anchor: قال العوفي، عن ابن عباس: لما نزل على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم القرآن، أبطأ عنه جبريل أياما،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425#2/r1.claim: God did not leave or hate the Prophet; the afterlife is better for him than worldly life, as shown by his asceticism and his choice to return to God rather than remain in the world.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425#2/r1.anchor: وقوله: {ما ودعك ربك} أي: ما تركك، {وما قلى} أي: وما أبغضك، {وللآخرة خير لك من الأولى} أي: والدار الآخرة خير لك من هذه الدار.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425#2/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425#2/r2.claim: The Prophet compares himself and worldly life to a traveler who rests briefly under a tree's shade and then moves on; Tirmidhi grades the report hasan sahih.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425#2/r2.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ما لي وللدنيا؟! ما أنا والدنيا؟! إنما مثلي ومثل الدنيا كراكب ظل تحت شجرة، ثم راح وتركتها

JISHUMI:v10p7449/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7449/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7449/r3.claim: The common reading doubles the dāl in waddaʿaka, while some read it light; the senses are farewell and leaving.
JISHUMI:v10p7449/r3.anchor: قراءة العامة: (ما ودعك) بالتشديد من التوديع، وعن بعضهم بالتخفيف أي: ما تركك

JISHUMI:v10p7449/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7449/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7449/r10.claim: Tawdīʿ means parting or farewell, but here it is a metaphor: God does not withhold His customary favor, revelation, and support, contrary to the disbelievers' claim.
JISHUMI:v10p7449/r10.anchor: والتوديع: المفارقة والتبرك، ودع يودع توديعا، وهو في هذا الموضع استعارة

KASHSHAF:93:3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:93:3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:93:3/r1.claim: The clause answers the oath and means God has not abandoned the Prophet like someone who takes leave.
KASHSHAF:93:3/r1.anchor: جواب القسم . ومعناه : ما قطعك قطع المودع

KASHSHAF:93:3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:93:3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:93:3/r2.claim: A lighter reading of waddaʿaka means simply that God did not leave the Prophet.

KASHSHAF:93:3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:93:3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:93:3/r3.claim: The poem's verb waddaʿnā means 'we left,' evidence for the usage of wadaʿ.

KASHSHAF:93:3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:93:3/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:93:3/r4.claim: Tawdiʿ intensifies leaving: a person who bids farewell while departing has emphatically left you.
KASHSHAF:93:3/r4.anchor: مبالغة في الودع ؛ لأنّ من ودّعك مفارقاً فقد بالغ في تركك

KASHSHAF:93:3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:93:3/r5.speaker: المشركون
KASHSHAF:93:3/r5.claim: When revelation was delayed for days, the polytheists said Muhammad's Lord had abandoned and hated him.
KASHSHAF:93:3/r5.anchor: فقال المشركون : إنّ محمداً ودّعه ربه وقلاه

KASHSHAF:93:3/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:93:3/r6.speaker: أم جميل امرأة أبي لهب
KASHSHAF:93:3/r6.claim: Another occasion report says Umm Jamil told Muhammad that his devil had left him, after which the sura was revealed.
KASHSHAF:93:3/r6.anchor: وقيل : إنّ أم جميل امرأة أبي لهب قالت له : يا محمد

KASHSHAF:93:3/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:93:3/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:93:3/r7.claim: The pronoun is omitted after qalā, as in al-dhākirāt and the shortened sequence 'sheltered, guided, enriched,' because the omitted object is obvious.
KASHSHAF:93:3/r7.anchor: في قوله : { والذاكرين الله كثيراً والذاكرات }

SAMIN-DURR:93:3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:93:3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:93:3/r1.claim: ‘Ma wadda‘aka’ is the oath’s answer; the common reading doubles dāl from tawdi‘, while ‘Urwa, his son Hisham, Abu Haywa, and Ibn Abi ‘Abla read a light dāl from wada‘ (‘leave’).
SAMIN-DURR:93:3/r1.anchor: والعامة على تشديد الدال من التوديع

SAMIN-DURR:93:3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:93:3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:93:3/r2.claim: Although standard Arabic generally uses taraka in place of wada‘ and its derivatives, the verb occurs in poetry; two anonymous poems demonstrate it.
SAMIN-DURR:93:3/r2.anchor: والمشهور في اللغة الاستغناء عن ودع ووذر واسم فاعلهما

SAMIN-DURR:93:3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:93:3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:93:3/r3.claim: One explanation says tawdi‘ intensifies wada‘, since someone who bids farewell while leaving has emphatically abandoned the person.
SAMIN-DURR:93:3/r3.anchor: قيل: والتوديع مبالغة في الودع؛ لأن من ودعك مفارقا فقد بالغ في تركك

SAMIN-DURR:93:3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:93:3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:93:3/r4.claim: ‘Ma qala’ means ‘he did not hate you’; the usual imperfect qalahu has kasra, while Tayyi’ uses fatḥa, and a poem witnesses the latter.
SAMIN-DURR:93:3/r4.anchor: قلاه يقليه بكسر العين في المضارع، وطيىء تقول: قلاه يقلاه بالفتح

SAMIN-DURR:93:3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:93:3/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:93:3/r5.claim: The object of ‘qala’ is omitted because it is understood, and for the verse cadence; the same ellipsis follows ‘fa-awa’ and what comes after it.
SAMIN-DURR:93:3/r5.anchor: وحذف مفعول " قلى " مراعاة للفواصل مع العلم به وكذا بعد " فآوى

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p292/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p292/r1.speaker: جندب
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p292/r1.claim: Al-Aswad ibn Qays reports from Jundub that after the Prophet's finger was struck and bled, he recited a couplet about it; after he stopped rising for prayer for two or three nights, a woman said his devil had left him, and the verse was revealed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p292/r1.anchor: عن جندب أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم رمي بحجر في إصبعه فدميت , فقال : هل أنت إلا أصبع دميت

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p292/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p292/r2.speaker: عائشة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p292/r2.claim: Hisham reports from Urwa, from his father, that Gabriel's delay distressed the Prophet; Aisha says Quraysh unbelievers claimed his Lord had forsaken him, prompting the revelation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p292/r2.anchor: قالت عائشة : فقال كفار قريش : إنا نرى ربك قد قلاك , مما رأوا من جزعه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p292/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p292/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p292/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Gabriel was absent for twelve nights, so the polytheists said God had abandoned Muhammad, and this verse was revealed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p292/r3.anchor: روى ابن جريج أن جبريل لبث عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم اثنا عشرة ليلة فقال المشركون : لقد ودع محمدا ربه , فنزلت

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p292/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p292/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p292/r4.claim: The common doubled reading of ودعك means revelation did not cease in order to bid the Prophet farewell; the lighter reading means God did not leave him in aversion.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p292/r4.anchor: قراءة الجمهور ودعك , بالتشديد , ومعناها : ما انقطع الوحي عنك توديعا لك .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p292/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p292/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p292/r5.claim: Mawardi glosses وما قلى as God did not hate the Prophet, and introduces a supporting line by al-Akhtal.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p292/r5.anchor: ( وما قلى ) أي ما أبغضك , قال الأخطل :

MUQATIL:93:1-6/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:93:1-6/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:93:1-6/r2.claim: Gabriel's revelation stopped for forty days, though another report says three; Meccan polytheists taunted Muhammad that God had abandoned him, while Muslims also asked about the delay.
MUQATIL:93:1-6/r2.anchor: وذلك أن حبريل، عليه السلام، لم ينزل على محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم أربعين يوما، ويقال: ثلاثة أيام

MUQATIL:93:1-6/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:93:1-6/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:93:1-6/r3.claim: The Prophet told those asking about revelation that Gabriel could not descend while they neglected cleaning their knuckles and trimming their nails.
MUQATIL:93:1-6/r3.anchor: كيف ينزل على الوحي، وأنتم لا تنقون براجمكم، ولا تقلمون أظفاركم

MUQATIL:93:1-6/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:93:1-6/r4.speaker: جبريل عليه السلام
MUQATIL:93:1-6/r4.claim: When Gabriel returned, Muhammad said he had longed for him; Gabriel replied that he longed more for Muhammad's honor with God but was a commanded servant, citing 19:64.
MUQATIL:93:1-6/r4.anchor: أنا كنت إليك أشد شوقا لكرامتك على الله عز وجل، ولكني عبد مأمور

MUQATIL:93:1-6/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:93:1-6/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:93:1-6/r5.claim: In 19:64, what is before refers to worldly life, what is behind to the afterlife, and what is between them to the forty years between the two blasts; God has not forgotten Muhammad.
MUQATIL:93:1-6/r5.anchor: وما نتنزل إلا بأمر ربك له ما بين أيدينا من الدنيا وما خلفنا من الآخرة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p344#8/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p344#8/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p344#8/r1.claim: God has not left the Prophet since choosing him or hated him since loving him; tawaḍīʿ intensifies the sense of leaving.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p344#8/r1.anchor: ما تركك منذ اختارك وما أبغضك منذ أحبك والتوديع مبالغة فى الودع لأن من ودعك مفارقا فقد بالغ فى تركك

NASAFI-FULL:v4p344#8/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p344#8/r2.speaker: المشركون
NASAFI-FULL:v4p344#8/r2.claim: After revelation paused for days, the polytheists said Muhammad's Lord had abandoned and hated him; this report occasioned the revelation.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p344#8/r2.anchor: روى أن الوحى تأخر عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أياما فقال المشركون أن محمدا ودعه ربه وقلاه فنزلت

NASAFI-FULL:v4p344#8/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p344#8/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p344#8/r3.claim: The object pronoun is omitted from qalaa just as it is omitted from the feminine participle in a cited verse and from the following verbs of the same surah; this is concise omission because the referent is clear.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p344#8/r3.anchor: وحذف الضمير من قلى كحذفه من الذاكرات وقوله والذاكرين الله كثيرا والذاكرات يريد والذاكراته ونحوه فاوى فهدى فأغنى وهو اختصار لفظى لظهور المحذوف

QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r16.claim: The statement that God neither abandoned nor hated the Prophet answers the oath.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r16.anchor: { ما ودعك ربك }: هذا جواب القسم.

QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r17.claim: When Gabriel's coming paused, polytheists claimed God had abandoned and hated Muhammad, reasoning that revelation should have continued as for earlier prophets.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r17.anchor: فقال المشركون: قلاه الله وودعه فنزلت الآية.

QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r18.speaker: ابن جريج
QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r18.claim: Ibn Jurayj says revelation was withheld from the Prophet for twelve days.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r18.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: احتبس عنه الوحي اثني عشر يوما.

QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r19.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r19.claim: Ibn Abbas gives fifteen days for the interval without revelation.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r19.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: خمسة عشر يوما.

QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r20.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r20.claim: Muqatil gives forty days for the interval; another report gives twenty-five.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r20.anchor: وقيل: خمسة وعشرين يوما. وقال مقاتل: أربعين يوما.

QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r21.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r21.speaker: البخاري عن جندب بن سفيان
QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r21.claim: Bukhari transmits from Jundub ibn Sufyan that the Prophet was ill and missed night worship for two or three nights before a woman mocked him, prompting the revelation.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r21.anchor: وفي البخاري عن جندب بن سفيان قال: اشتكى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فلم يقم ليلتين أو ثلاثا

QURTUBI-FULL:93:3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3/r1.speaker: جندب البجلي
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3/r1.claim: Jundub al-Bajali reports that in a cave the Prophet's finger bled; he recited a couplet about an injured finger in God's path, then Gabriel's delay drew the polytheists' taunt.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3/r1.anchor: عن جندب البجلي قال: كنت مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في غار فدميت إصبعه، فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:93:3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3/r2.speaker: الترمذي
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3/r2.claim: Al-Tirmidhi grades the Jundub report Hasan Sahih.

QURTUBI-FULL:93:3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3/r3.claim: Al-Tirmidhi omitted the detail that the Prophet did not rise for two or three nights; Bukhari includes it, and Qurtubi calls that account the soundest.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3/r3.anchor: لم يذكر الترمذي: " فلم يقم ليلتين أو ثلاثا " أسقطه الترمذي. وذكره البخاري، وهو أصح ما قيل في ذلك.

QURTUBI-FULL:93:3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3/r4.speaker: الثعلبي عن جندب بن سفيان
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3/r4.claim: Al-Tha'labi transmits that a stone bloodied the Prophet's finger, he stopped night worship for two or three nights, and Umm Jamil mocked the absence of his devil before the surah descended.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3/r4.anchor: فمكث ليلتين أو ثلاثا لا يقوم الليل. فقالت له أم جميل امرأة أبي لهب:

QURTUBI-FULL:93:3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3/r5.speaker: أبو عمران الجوني
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3/r5.claim: Abu Imran al-Jawni says Gabriel's delay distressed the Prophet as he prayed at the Kaaba; Gabriel touched his shoulders and delivered the verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3/r5.anchor: أبطأ جبريل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى شق عليه فجاء وهو واضع جبهته على الكعبة

QURTUBI-FULL:93:3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3/r6.speaker: خولة
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3/r6.claim: Khawla says a dead puppy hidden beneath a bed kept Gabriel away for days; after she removed it, Gabriel came and explained angels do not enter a house containing a dog or image.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3/r6.anchor: إن جروا دخل البيت، فدخل تحت السرير فمات، فمكث نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أياما لا ينزل عليه الوحي.

QURTUBI-FULL:93:3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3/r7.claim: Another account says revelation paused after the Prophet promised Jews an answer about the Spirit, Dhu al-Qarnayn, and the Cave Companions without saying if God wills.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3/r7.anchor: لما سألته اليهود عن الروح وذي القرنين وأصحاب الكهف قال: «سأخبركم غدا» ولم يقل إن شاء الله.

QURTUBI-FULL:93:3#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3#2/r1.claim: One report has Muslims ask about the delay; Gabriel says their unclean knuckles, untrimmed nails, and moustaches kept him away, then explains he is an obedient messenger who comes by command.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3#2/r1.anchor: «وكيف ينزل علي وأنتم لا تنقون رواجبكم وفي رواية براجمكم ولا تقصون أظفاركم ولا تأخذون من شواربكم». فنزل جبريل بهذه السورة

QURTUBI-FULL:93:3#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3#2/r2.claim: In the same report the Prophet and Gabriel express mutual longing, and the revelation says angels descend only by their Lord's command.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3#2/r2.anchor: فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ما جئت حتى اشتقت إليك» فقال جبريل: «وأنا كنت أشد إليك شوقا، ولكني عبد مأمور»

QURTUBI-FULL:93:3#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3#2/r3.claim: The common reading has the doubled consonant and evokes a farewell; Ibn Abbas and Ibn al-Zubayr read the verb lightly to mean left.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3#2/r3.anchor: «ودعك» بالتشديد: قراءة العامة، من التوديع، وذلك كتوديع المفارق. وروي عن ابن عباس وابن الزبير أنهما قرأاه

QURTUBI-FULL:93:3#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3#2/r4.speaker: المبرد محمد بن يزيد
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3#2/r4.claim: Al-Mubarrad says Arabs rarely use wada'a or wadhara because initial waw is weak, so they substitute taraka.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3#2/r4.anchor: قال المبرد محمد بن يزيد: لا يكادون يقولون ودع ولا وذر، لضعف الواو إذا قدمت، واستغنوا عنها بترك.

QURTUBI-FULL:93:3#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3#2/r5.claim: Ma qala means God has not hated the Prophet after loving him; the final pronoun is omitted because the clause ends the verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3#2/r5.anchor: { وما قلى } أي ما أبغضك ربك منذ أحبك. وترك الكاف، لأنه رأس آية.

QURTUBI-FULL:93:3#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3#2/r6.claim: Qila means hatred, with distinct vowelled forms; the Tayyi' dialect also says yaqla, and cited poems witness the forms.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3#2/r6.anchor: والقلى: البغض فإن فتحت القاف مددت تقول قلاه يقليه قلى وقلاء.

QURTUBI-FULL:93:3#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3#2/r7.speaker: ثعلب
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3#2/r7.claim: Tha'lab cites a line using naqla-ha to mean we do not hate her.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3#2/r7.anchor: وأنشد ثعلب: أيام أم الغمر لا نقلاها أي لا نبغضها.

QURTUBI-FULL:93:3#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3#2/r8.speaker: امرؤ القيس
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3#2/r8.claim: Imru' al-Qays uses muqalli for one who is hated, supplying another witness for the root.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3#2/r8.anchor:
وقال امرؤ القيس:
ولست بمقلي الخلال ولا قال

QURTUBI-FULL:93:3#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3#2/r9.claim: The full sense is that God neither abandoned nor hated the Prophet; dropping the second pronoun at a verse ending parallels a Qur'anic omission elsewhere.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:3#2/r9.anchor: وتأويل الآية: ما ودعك ربك وما قلاك. فترك الكاف لأنه رأس آية

QUTB-ZILAL:93:3/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:93:3/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:93:3/r1.claim: The verse directly denies that God left or shunned the Prophet, rejecting the claim intended to hurt and unsettle him.
QUTB-ZILAL:93:3/r1.anchor: ما تركك ربك ولا جافاك - كما زعم من يريدون إيذاء روحك

QUTB-ZILAL:93:3/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:93:3/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:93:3/r2.claim: Calling God “your Lord” affirms the Prophet’s belonging to Him and God’s care and guardianship over him.
QUTB-ZILAL:93:3/r2.anchor: وأنت عبده المنسوب إليه ، المضاف إلى ربوبيته

ZAJJAJ:v5p339/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p339/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p339/r3.claim: God neither stopped sending revelation nor hated the Prophet. Revelation paused for fifteen days, prompting people to say his companion had forsaken and hated him; the verse answered them.
ZAJJAJ:v5p339/r3.anchor: وذلك أنه تأخر الوحي عن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - خمسة عشر يوما،

ZAJJAJ:v5p339/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p339/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p339/r4.claim: The object “you” is omitted after qalā, as in the feminine form of “those who remember God often,” which likewise implies the object.
ZAJJAJ:v5p339/r4.anchor: كما قال: (والذاكرين الله كثيرا والذاكرات) المعنى والذاكراته (1).

RAZI-FULL:v31p190#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p190#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p190#2/r1.claim: Waddaʿaka derives from farewell; its lighter reading means He did not leave you, while qila means hatred and intensifies the idea of abandonment.
RAZI-FULL:v31p190#2/r1.anchor: ودعك من التوديع كما يودع المفارق

RAZI-FULL:v31p190#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p190#2/r2.speaker: الفراء
