RAZI:93:3/r1.claim: Abū ʿUbayda and al-Mubarrad derive the word from farewell at parting; the light reading means He did not leave you, while tawdīʿ intensifies the act of leaving.
RAZI:93:3/r1.anchor: أبو عبيدة والمبرد : ودعك من التوديع

RAZI:93:3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:93:3/r2.claim: Qilā means hatred; qalahu yaqlihi is used of hating someone.

RAZI:93:3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:3/r3.speaker: الفراء
RAZI:93:3/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ understands the clause as wa-mā qalāka, with the object pronoun omitted.

RAZI:93:3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:93:3/r4.claim: One explanation for omitting the second kāf is that the first kāf in waddaʿaka already supplies it.
RAZI:93:3/r4.anchor: حذفت الكاف اكتفاء بالكاف الأولى في ودعك

RAZI:93:3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:93:3/r5.claim: The omitted kāf also preserves the sūra's verse endings in yāʾ.

RAZI:93:3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:93:3/r6.claim: The unexpressed object can make the denial broad: God did not hate the Prophet's companions or anyone he loved through the Resurrection, affirming that one is with whom one loves.
RAZI:93:3/r6.anchor: فائدة الإطلاق أنه ما قلاك ولا

RAZI:93:3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:3/r7.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI:93:3/r7.claim: Exegetes report that Gabriel's arrival was delayed, so the polytheists said God had abandoned and hated the Prophet; the verse was revealed in response.

RAZI:93:3/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:3/r8.speaker: السدي
RAZI:93:3/r8.claim: Al-Suddī says the delay lasted forty nights; the Prophet complained to Khadīja, who suggested that his Lord might have forgotten or hated him.

RAZI:93:3/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:3/r9.speaker: أم جميل
RAZI:93:3/r9.claim: Umm Jamīl, Abū Lahab's wife, taunted the Prophet that his satan seemed to have left him.
RAZI:93:3/r9.anchor: إن أم جميل امرأة أبي لهب قالت له

RAZI:93:3/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:3/r10.speaker: الحسن
RAZI:93:3/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan reports that after revelation paused, the Prophet told Khadīja that his Lord had left and hated him; she denied this and said God began his honor to complete it.

RAZI:93:3/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:3/r11.speaker: الأصوليون
RAZI:93:3/r11.claim: The theologians of legal principles reject the report of the Prophet thinking God had left him, since he knew removing him from prophecy would violate divine wisdom and revelation's timing follows benefit.

RAZI:93:3/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:3/r12.speaker: author
RAZI:93:3/r12.claim: If the report about the Prophet's complaint is sound, Rāzī says it can mean he was testing Khadīja to reveal her understanding, or letting people recognize it.
RAZI:93:3/r12.anchor: ثم إن صح ذلك يحمل على أنه كان مقصوده عليه الصلاة والسلام أن يجربها ليعرف قدر علمها

RAZI:93:3/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:3/r13.speaker: ابن جريج
RAZI:93:3/r13.claim: Ibn Jurayj gives the period without revelation as twelve days.

RAZI:93:3/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:3/r14.speaker: الكلبي
RAZI:93:3/r14.claim: Al-Kalbī gives the period without revelation as fifteen days.

RAZI:93:3/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:3/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI:93:3/r15.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās gives the period without revelation as twenty-five days.

RAZI:93:3/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:3/r16.speaker: السدي ومقاتل
RAZI:93:3/r16.claim: Al-Suddī and Muqātil give the period without revelation as forty days.

RAZI:93:3/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:3/r17.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
RAZI:93:3/r17.claim: Most exegetes say the pause followed the Prophet's promise to answer the Jews about the Spirit, Dhū al-Qarnayn, and the Companions of the Cave without saying “if God wills.”
RAZI:93:3/r17.anchor: فذكر أكثر المفسرين أن اليهود سألت رسول الله

RAZI:93:3/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:3/r18.speaker: ابن زيد
RAZI:93:3/r18.claim: Ibn Zayd says a puppy kept at home for al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn caused the delay; Gabriel explained that angels do not enter a house containing a dog or image.
RAZI:93:3/r18.anchor: ابن زيد : السبب فيه كون جرو في بيته

RAZI:93:3/r19.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:3/r19.speaker: جندب بن سفيان
RAZI:93:3/r19.claim: Jundub ibn Sufyān says a stone struck the Prophet's finger; he recited a couplet about a bleeding finger in God's path, after which revelation paused.
RAZI:93:3/r19.anchor: جندب بن سفيان : رمى النبي عليه الصلاة بحجر

RAZI:93:3/r20.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:3/r20.speaker: author
RAZI:93:3/r20.claim: An unattributed report mentions someone among them who did not trim his nails, in the discussion of the revelation pause.
RAZI:93:3/r20.anchor: وروي أنه كان فيهم من لا يقلم الأظفار وههنا سؤالان

RAZI:93:3/r21.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:3/r21.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI:93:3/r21.claim: A report says the Prophet told Gabriel he had missed him, and Gabriel replied that he longed even more but was commanded, citing 19:64.
RAZI:93:3/r21.anchor: وروي أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قال لجبريل

RAZI:93:3/r22.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:3/r22.speaker: author
RAZI:93:3/r22.claim: The delay need show only that the Prophet missed what was preferable, not that he was hated; a person who misses the best is not thereby detested.
RAZI:93:3/r22.anchor: أقصى ما في الباب أن ذلك كان تركا للأفضل والأولى

RAZI:93:3/r23.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:3/r23.speaker: author
RAZI:93:3/r23.claim: Assuring a beloved person that he is not hated would be odd without cause, but it honors him when enemies have spread that charge and he is distressed by it.
RAZI:93:3/r23.anchor: إذا ألقوا في الألسنة أن السلطان يبغضه

RAZI:93:3/r24.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:3/r24.speaker: author
RAZI:93:3/r24.claim: The revelation's pause demonstrates that the Qurʾān comes from God: if it originated with the Prophet, it would not have been withheld from him.
RAZI:93:3/r24.anchor: هذه الواقعة تدل على أن القرآن من عند الله

TAB:93:3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:93:3/r1.speaker: author
TAB:93:3/r1.claim: As the answer to the oath, the verse assures Muḥammad that his Lord has neither abandoned nor hated him.
TAB:93:3/r1.anchor: وقوله :  ما وَدّعَكَ رَبّكَ وَما قَلى وهذا جواب القسم ،   ومعناه :  ما تركك يا محمد ربك وما أبغضك .

TAB:93:3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:93:3/r2.speaker: author
TAB:93:3/r2.claim: The object pronoun in “nor hated” is omitted because the preceding “abandoned you” makes the addressee and meaning clear.
TAB:93:3/r2.anchor: وقيل :  وَما قَلى ومعناه :  وما قلاك ،   اكتفاء بفهم السامع لمعناه ،   إذ كان قد تقدّم ذلك قولُه :

TAB:93:3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:93:3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:93:3/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains that God did not leave Muḥammad or hate him.
TAB:93:3/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   في قوله :  ما وَدّعَكَ رَبّكَ وَما قَلى يقول :  ما تركك ربك ،   وما أبغضك .

TAB:93:3/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:93:3/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB:93:3/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says qālā means “hated you” and identifies al-qālī as the one who hates.
TAB:93:3/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد ،   في قوله :  ما وَدّعَكَ رَبّكَ وَما قَلى قال :  ما قلاك ربك وما أبغضك قال :  والقالي :  المبغض .

TAB:93:3/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:93:3/r5.speaker: جندب بن عبد الله البجلي
TAB:93:3/r5.claim: Jundub reports that the pause in Gabriel's visits prompted a woman or the Meccan polytheists to say Muḥammad had been abandoned; versions call the absent companion a satan, and al-Ṭabarī identifies Ibn ʿAbd Allāh as Jundub.
TAB:93:3/r5.anchor: عن الأسود بن قيس ،   أنه سمع جندبا البَجَليّ قال :  قالت امرأة لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :  ما أرى صاحبك

TAB:93:3/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:93:3/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن شداد
TAB:93:3/r6.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaddād reports that Khadīja told the Prophet his Lord seemed to have forsaken him, after which the verse was revealed.
TAB:93:3/r6.anchor: عن عبد الله بن شدّاد أن خديجة قالت للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم :  ما أرى ربك إلا قد قلاك ،   فأنزل الله

TAB:93:3/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:93:3/r7.speaker: عروة بن الزبير
TAB:93:3/r7.claim: ʿUrwa says Gabriel's delay greatly distressed the Prophet, and Khadīja then said his Lord seemed to dislike him before the sūra came down.
TAB:93:3/r7.anchor: عن هشام بن عروة ،   عن أبيه ،   قال :  أبطأ جبريل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ،   فجزع جزعا شديدا ،   وقالت خديجة

TAB:93:3/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:93:3/r8.speaker: قتادة
TAB:93:3/r8.claim: Qatāda says people in Mecca claimed the Prophet's companion had hated and abandoned him because Gabriel had delayed the revelation.
TAB:93:3/r8.anchor: عن قتادة ما وَدّعَكَ رَبّكَ وَما قَلى قال :  إن جبريل عليه السلام أبطأ عليه بالوحي ،   فقال ناس من الناس

TAB:93:3/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:93:3/r9.speaker: الضحاك
TAB:93:3/r9.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says Gabriel stayed away from Muḥammad, leading the polytheists to claim his Lord had abandoned and hated him.
TAB:93:3/r9.anchor: سمعت الضحاك يقول في قوله :  ما وَدّعَكَ رَبّكَ وَما قَلى مكث جبريل عن محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ،   فقال المشركون

TAB:93:3/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:93:3/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:93:3/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Gabriel delayed for several days after the Qurʾān first came, and the polytheists taunted the Prophet before this reassurance descended.
TAB:93:3/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس :  ما وَدّعَكَ رَبّكَ وَما قَلى قال :  لما نزل عليه القرآن ،   أبطأ عنه جبريل أياما ،   فعُيّر بذلك

ITQAN:v2p339#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p339#2/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p339#2/r2.claim: The phrase means that your Lord did not leave you or hate you.
ITQAN:v2p339#2/r2.anchor: ﴿ ما ودعك ربك وما قلى ﴾ ما تركك وما أبغضك

BURHAN:v3p167/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p167/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p167/r2.claim: In “ما قلى,” the object is omitted to preserve the verse endings in alif.
BURHAN:v3p167/r2.anchor: فحذف المفعول لأن فواصل الآي على الألف

ITQAN:v3p154/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p154/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p154/r5.claim: A word may be omitted to preserve the verse ending: wa-mā qalā means wa-mā qalāka, 'nor has He forsaken you.'
ITQAN:v3p154/r5.anchor: ومنها رعاية الفاصلة نحو ﴿ ما ودعك ربك وما قلى ﴾ أي ( وما قلاك )

ITQAN:v1p94#3/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p94#3/r3.speaker: جندب
ITQAN:v1p94#3/r3.claim: The Two Sahihs and others transmit from Jundub that after the Prophet was ill and missed prayer for a night or two, a woman said his devil had abandoned him, and the Duha verses were revealed.
ITQAN:v1p94#3/r3.anchor: مثاله ما أخرجه الشيخان وغيرهما عن جندب اشتكى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فلم يقم ليلة أو ليلتين

ITQAN:v3p268/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p268/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p268/r1.claim: One ellipsis omits the object of the verb, as in 'gave and was mindful' and 'nor did He reject you.'
ITQAN:v3p268/r1.anchor: التاسع عشر حذف المفعول نحو ﴿ فأما من أعطى واتقى ﴾ ﴿ ما ودعك ربك وما قلى ﴾

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p250/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p250/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p250/r1.claim: The daily transition from bright duha to a still night does not suggest that heaven has abandoned earth; likewise, a pause after revelation does not mean God abandoned or hated Muhammad.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p250/r1.anchor: الواو لافتة إلى صورة مادية وواقع حسي، يشهد به الناس تألق الضوء في ضحوة النهار

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p91/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p91/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p91/r1.claim: In 93:3, directly naming the Prophet in ما ودعك honors him, while omitting him as the object of قلى avoids directly associating him with hatred; mention and omission both honor him.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p91/r1.anchor: فلم يقل (وما قلاك) حتى لا يكون الخطاب مباشرة للرسول

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p541/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p541/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p541/r1.claim: God names the Prophet in denying the loving act of farewell, honoring him, but omits the object after قلى so the beloved Prophet is not directly cast as hated.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1098/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1098/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1098/r3.claim: Mentioning the object in ما ودعك honors the Prophet because farewell is between beloved people; omitting it after وما قلى avoids directly naming him as the object of hatred.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1098/r3.anchor: الحذف (وما قلى) فيه إكرام للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

NASHR:v2p407/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p407/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
NASHR:v2p407/r3.claim: Al-Awfi reports from Ibn Abbas that Gabriel's delay distressed the Prophet, prompting the polytheists to say his Lord had abandoned and hated him; God answered with al-Duha's reassurance.
NASHR:v2p407/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس - رضي الله عنهما - لما نزل على رسول الله

NASHR:v2p405#3/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p405#3/r7.speaker: جندب بن عبد الله البجلي
NASHR:v2p405#3/r7.claim: Jundub reports in the two Ṣaḥīḥs that illness kept the Prophet from rising one or two nights and a woman said his Satan had left; another version says Gabriel was late and the polytheists said Muhammad was abandoned, then al-Duha came.
NASHR:v2p405#3/r7.anchor: في الصحيحين من حديث جندب بن عبد الله البجلي رضي الله عنه: اشتكى النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فلم يقم ليلة، أو ليلتين

IBNASHUR:93:1/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:93:1/r3.speaker: جندب بن سفيان البجلي
IBNASHUR:93:1/r3.claim: In the Ṣaḥīḥayn account, Jundub reports that the Prophet injured his finger and was unwell and did not rise at night for two or three nights; Umm Jamīl, identified through Ibn ʿAbbās by Ibn ʿAṭiyya as Abū Lahab's wife, taunted him that his devil had left, and the verses were revealed.
IBNASHUR:93:1/r3.anchor: عن الأسود بن قيس عن جندب بن سفيان البجلي قال  دميت إصبع رسول الله

IBNASHUR:93:1/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:93:1/r4.speaker: جندب البجلي
IBNASHUR:93:1/r4.claim: In al-Tirmidhī's report, Jundub recalls being with the Prophet in a cave when his finger bled; after Gabriel's delay, polytheists said the Prophet had been abandoned. Al-Tirmidhī grades the report ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
IBNASHUR:93:1/r4.anchor: عن الأسود عن جندب البجلي قال  كنت مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في غار

IBNKATHIR:93:1/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:93:1/r11.speaker: جندب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:93:1/r11.claim: Jundub reports that after the Prophet was ill and missed prayer for one or two nights, a woman said his Satan had left him, and God revealed al-Ḍuḥā and the following reassurance.
IBNKATHIR:93:1/r11.anchor: عن الأسود بن قيس قال : سمعت جندبا يقول : اشتكى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فلم يقم ليلة أو ليلتين

IBNKATHIR:93:1/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:93:1/r12.speaker: جندب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:93:1/r12.claim: In another narration, Gabriel was delayed and the polytheists said Muhammad had been abandoned; the revelation answered them that his Lord had not abandoned or detested him.
IBNKATHIR:93:1/r12.anchor: وفي رواية سفيان بن عيينة عن الأسود بن قيس : سمع جندبا قال : أبطأ جبريل على رسول الله

IBNKATHIR:93:1/r13.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:93:1/r13.speaker: جندب
IBNKATHIR:93:1/r13.claim: A report says a stone cut the Prophet's finger; after he did not rise for two or three nights, a woman said his Satan had left him, then the sūra was revealed.
IBNKATHIR:93:1/r13.anchor: أنه سمع جندبا يقول : رمي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بحجر في أصبعه

IBNKATHIR:93:1/r14.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:93:1/r14.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:93:1/r14.claim: Ibn Kathir says the poetic line about the Prophet's bleeding finger is authentic in both Ṣaḥīḥ collections, but calls it unusual to make the injury the cause of his missed prayers and the sūra's revelation.
IBNKATHIR:93:1/r14.anchor: ولكن الغريب هاهنا جعله سببا لتركه القيام ،   ونزول هذه السورة

IBNKATHIR:93:1/r15.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:93:1/r15.speaker: قيل
IBNKATHIR:93:1/r15.claim: One account identifies the woman who said the Prophet's Satan had left him as Umm Jamīl, the wife of Abū Lahab.
IBNKATHIR:93:1/r15.anchor: قيل : إن هذه المرأة هي : أم جميل امرأة أبي لهب

IBNKATHIR:93:1/r16.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:93:1/r16.speaker: خديجة
IBNKATHIR:93:1/r16.claim: Two reports from Ibn Jarīr say Khadīja told the Prophet that she thought his Lord had forsaken him; Ibn Kathir notes both are mursal and suggests her attribution may be unpreserved or an expression of sorrow.
IBNKATHIR:93:1/r16.anchor: ولعل ذكر خديجة ليس محفوظا ،   أو قالته على وجه التأسف والتحزن

IBNKATHIR:93:1/r18.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:93:1/r18.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR:93:1/r18.claim: Al-ʿAwfī reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that when revelation paused for days and polytheists said God had abandoned and detested Muhammad, this reassurance was revealed.

BURHAN:v3p318/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p318/r7.speaker: ابن الشجري
BURHAN:v3p318/r7.claim: Ibn al-Shajarī counts “nor did He forsake” as a shift to third person; the author rejects this, analyzing it instead as an omitted object.
BURHAN:v3p318/r7.anchor: وجعل منه ابن الشجري ﴿ ما ودعك ربك وما قلى ﴾
